Hero.title: Building a Progressive Nepal
Hero.description: I am Janardan Sharma 'Pravakar', the ideological guide of the Progressive Democratic Party and former Deputy Secretary General of the Maoist Centre. Having served as Finance Minister, Home Minister, and Energy Minister of Nepal, I worked to end the energy crisis, ensure economic stability, and strengthen the peace process. My main goal is inclusive nationalism, economic self-reliance, youth empowerment, and social justice – which I am advancing through a youth-led progressive campaign.

BioTeaser.title: A Life Dedicated to the People
BioTeaser.p1: Janardan Sharma 'Pravakar' is a prominent political figure in Nepal, known for his dynamic leadership and unwavering commitment to the nation's progress.
BioTeaser.p2: From his early involvement in student movements to leading key ministries, his journey reflects a deep dedication to social justice, federalism, and economic prosperity.

Biography.title: Janardan Sharma 'Pravakar'
Biography.subtitle: A leader forged in struggle, dedicated to peace, and committed to the prosperity of Nepal.
Biography.introP1: Janardan Sharma, popularly known by his nom de guerre 'Pravakar', is a visionary leader and a key architect of Nepal's political transformation. From the rugged hills of Rukum to the corridors of Singha Durbar, his journey is a testament to resilience and unwavering commitment to the people.
Biography.introP2: As a prominent leader of the Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist Centre), he played a crucial role in the People's War, the peace process, and the drafting of the federal democratic republican constitution.
Biography.contribution1Desc: As Minister of Energy, he led the historic campaign to eliminate chronic power cuts, revolutionizing the energy sector.
Biography.contribution2Desc: Played a vital role in the integration of Maoist combatants and the management of arms, ensuring a smooth transition to peace.
Biography.contribution3Desc: A fierce advocate for federalism, ensuring rights and representation for marginalized communities and remote regions.
Biography.personalText: Beyond politics, Janardan Sharma is known for his literary interests, often expressing his thoughts through poetry and articles. He remains deeply connected to his roots in Rukum, frequently visiting and engaging with local communities to understand their evolving needs.

timeline.energySummary: Led the 'Ujyalo Nepal' campaign, successfully ending years of chronic load-shedding.
timeline.energyDetailP1: As the Minister for Energy, Janardan Sharma, along with the appointed Managing Director of the Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA) Kul Man Ghising, led an "uninterrupted power supply campaign" (often referred to as ending load shedding) through a combination of managerial, technical, and policy changes. The ministry's efforts focused on optimum utilization of existing resources and systemic reforms.
timeline.energyStep1Desc: A crucial step was the appointment of Kul Man Ghising as the Managing Director of the NEA in September 2016. The political leadership from the Ministry provided essential backing for the management to implement tough reforms.
timeline.energyStep2Desc: The core strategy involved efficient management and equitable distribution of the available electricity supply. This included balancing loads across different substations and prioritizing domestic supply over certain industrial demands during peak hours.
timeline.energyStep3Desc: The Ministry and NEA stopped the practice of announcing prolonged load-shedding schedules for major cities like Kathmandu Valley, making a commitment to not increase power cuts.
timeline.energyStep4Desc: The plan involved a directive to speed up the completion of critical infrastructure projects, notably the Khimti-Dhalkebar 220 kV transmission line, which was essential for bringing more power into the grid.
timeline.energyStep5Desc: Efforts were initiated to check and reduce high levels of power leakage (technical and commercial losses) within the distribution system.
timeline.energyStep6Desc: The strategy involved optimizing electricity imports from neighboring India to cover the domestic demand-supply gap.
timeline.energyStep7Desc: The Ministry introduced a 37-point work plan aimed at resolving the energy crisis, which included focusing on the completion of under-construction hydropower projects and seeking alternative energy sources like solar.
timeline.energyStep8Desc: Sharma initiated the "Nepal's Water, People's Investment" (नेपालको पानी, जनताको लगानी) campaign to encourage domestic investment in the energy sector.
timeline.energyStep9Desc: Sharma highlighted that addressing deep-seated issues of mismanagement, corruption, and inefficiency within the power sector was key to the reforms.
timeline.energyConclusion: These collective actions led to the elimination of the chronic load shedding that Nepal had experienced for decades, with the Ministry declaring load shedding a "subject of history".
